questions.topic: Points of trisection
questions.question: If P and Q are points of trisection of line segment joining A and B (in the order A, P, Q, B), then ratio of AP : AB is
questions.solution: (d) 1 : 3. Trisection points divide AB into three equal parts, so AP = AB/3 and AP : AB = 1 : 3.

questions.topic: Conformability for multiplication and addition
questions.question:
If A = [[5, 4], [3, −1]], B = [[0, 0], [0, 1]] and C = [[2], [1]] (a 2×1 column matrix). Which of the following statements are true?
Statement I: (A + B) × C is not possible.
Statement II: BA + C is possible.
questions.solution: (d) neither I nor II. A + B is 2×2 and C is 2×1, so (A + B)C is possible (order 2×1) – Statement I is false. BA is 2×2 and C is 2×1; matrices of different orders cannot be added, so BA + C is not possible – Statement II is false. (The handwritten key computes the orders but does not print a letter; verified answer is (d).)

questions.topic: Consecutive terms of an AP
questions.question:
Assertion (A): If 2k − 1, 4k − 3, 4k + 1 are three consecutive terms of an AP, then k = 1.
Reason (R): If a, b, c are three consecutive terms of an AP then 2b = a + c.

options.a: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A)
options.b: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true but reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A)
options.c: A is true, R is false
options.d: A is false, R is true

questions.solution: (d) A is false, R is true. Using 2b = a + c: 2(4k − 3) = (2k − 1) + (4k + 1) ⇒ 8k − 6 = 6k ⇒ k = 3, not 1. So A is false; R is the true property of an AP.

marking_points.point: 2(4k − 3) = (2k − 1) + (4k + 1) gives k = 3, so A is false and R is true → option (d)

questions.topic: Real roots of two equations simultaneously
questions.question: If the roots of the equations ax² + 2bx + c = 0 and bx² − 2√(ac) x + b = 0 are real, then which of the following conditions will satisfy both the above equations.
questions.solution: (b) b² = ac. First equation: D = 4b² − 4ac ≥ 0 ⇒ b² ≥ ac. Second: D = 4ac − 4b² ≥ 0 ⇒ b² ≤ ac. Both hold only when b² = ac.

questions.topic: sec θ − tan θ from sec θ + tan θ
questions.question: If sec θ + tan θ = M, then sec θ − tan θ is equal to:
questions.solution: (a) 1/M. sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 ⇒ (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1 ⇒ sec θ − tan θ = 1/M.

questions.topic: Largest cylinder cut from a cube
questions.question: The volume of the largest cylinder that can be drilled out of a cube of side 2r is
questions.solution: (b) 2πr³. The largest cylinder has radius r (half the side) and height 2r, so V = πr² × 2r = 2πr³.

questions.topic: Cyclic quadrilateral, tangent: alternate segment theorem
questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral in the circle with centre O. ST is a tangent to the circle at point B. ∠OBD = 25° and ∠CBT = 30°. Find: (a) ∠BCD (b) ∠ODC.
questions.solution:
(a) OB = OD (radii), so ∠ODB = ∠OBD = 25°. In ΔOBD, ∠BOD = 180° − 25° − 25° = 130°. C lies on the minor arc BD, so ∠BCD = ½ × reflex ∠BOD = ½ × (360° − 130°) = 115°. [Equivalently ∠BAD = ½ × 130° = 65° and ∠BCD = 180° − 65° = 115°, opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral.]
(b) ∠CDB = ∠CBT = 30° (angle between tangent and chord equals angle in the alternate segment). ∠ODC = ∠ODB + ∠BDC = 25° + 30° = 55°.
questions.figure_desc: Circle with centre O and cyclic quadrilateral ABCD (A at top, D right, C lower right, B lower left); OB and OD drawn with ∠OBD = 25°; tangent ST at B with ∠CBT = 30°.

questions.topic: Vertical line, point-slope form, intersection
questions.question:
In the given diagram, PQ ⊥ x-axis. R(0, 5) and Q(4, 0). (R lies on the y-axis, Q on the x-axis, and P is directly above Q, joined to R.)
(a) Find the equation of line PQ.
(b) If slope of PR is 3, find the equation of line PR.
(c) Find the coordinates of P.
questions.solution:
(a) PQ is perpendicular to the x-axis through Q(4, 0), so its equation is x = 4.
(b) PR passes through R(0, 5) with slope 3: y − 5 = 3(x − 0) ⇒ 3x − y + 5 = 0 (y = 3x + 5).
(c) P lies on x = 4 and on PR: y = 3(4) + 5 = 17. P = (4, 17).

questions.topic: Find unknown coefficient and factorise cubic
questions.question: If (x − 2) is a factor of 2x³ − x² − px − 2 then, find the value of 'p'. Hence, factorise the given polynomial completely.
questions.solution: f(x) = 2x³ − x² − px − 2. Since (x − 2) is a factor, f(2) = 0: 16 − 4 − 2p − 2 = 0 ⇒ 10 − 2p = 0 ⇒ p = 5. So f(x) = 2x³ − x² − 5x − 2. Dividing by (x − 2): quotient 2x² + 3x + 1. 2x² + 3x + 1 = 2x² + 2x + x + 1 = (2x + 1)(x + 1). Hence f(x) = (x − 2)(x + 1)(2x + 1).

questions.topic: Three terms of GP becoming AP
questions.question: The product of first three terms of a GP is 512. When 2 is added to its second term, the three terms form an AP. Find the numbers.
questions.solution: Let the terms be a/r, a, ar. Product = a³ = 512 ⇒ a = 8. Terms: 8/r, 8, 8r. After adding 2 to the middle term, 8/r, 10, 8r are in AP ⇒ 2(10) = 8/r + 8r ⇒ 20r = 8 + 8r² ⇒ 2r² − 5r + 2 = 0 ⇒ (r − 2)(2r − 1) = 0 ⇒ r = 2 or 1/2. r = 2: 4, 8, 16; r = 1/2: 16, 8, 4. The numbers are 4, 8, 16 (or 16, 8, 4).

marking_points.point: terms a/r, a, ar and a = 8

questions.topic: Surface area of solid cut into two halves (cone on cylinder)
questions.question:
A metallic solid (figure I), consisting of a cone mounted on a cylinder, is cut into two identical halves (figure II) along its height (as shown in the diagram). The diameter of the cylinder is 14 cm and the height is 30 cm. The height of the conical part is 24 cm. Find:
(a) the total surface area (both the halves).
(b) the total cost of painting the two halves at the rate of ₹20 per cm².
questions.solution:
r = 7 cm, H (cylinder) = 30 cm, h (cone) = 24 cm, l = √(7² + 24²) = √625 = 25 cm.
(a) TSA of both halves = CSA of cone + CSA of cylinder + area of base + 2 × (rectangular cut faces) + 2 × (triangular cut faces) = πrl + 2πrH + πr² + 2(14 × 30) + 2(½ × 14 × 24) = πr(l + 2H + r) + 840 + 336 = (22/7)(7)(25 + 60 + 7) + 1176 = 22 × 92 + 1176 = 2024 + 1176 = 3200 cm².
(b) Cost = 3200 × 20 = ₹64,000.

marking_points.point: curved surfaces + base = πr(l + 2H + r) = 2024 cm²

questions.figure_desc: Figure I: a cone on top of a cylinder with its vertical axis dotted; Figure II: the solid cut along the axis into two identical halves showing rectangular and triangular cut faces.

questions.topic: Loci: circle about a point and perpendicular bisector; circumcircle
questions.question:
Construct:
(a) an isosceles ΔABC in which AB = AC = 7 cm and BC = 6 cm.
(b) the locus of points such that it is 2.5 cm from the point A.
(c) the locus of points equidistant from B and C.
(d) Mark a point P closer to side BC which satisfies both the conditions mentioned in (b) and (c).
(e) a circle passing through P, B and C. Measure and record its radius.
questions.solution:
(a) Draw BC = 6 cm; with B and C as centres and radius 7 cm draw arcs meeting at A; join AB, AC.
(b) Locus of points 2.5 cm from A: a circle with centre A and radius 2.5 cm.
(c) Locus of points equidistant from B and C: the perpendicular bisector of BC (it passes through A since AB = AC).
(d) The perpendicular bisector cuts the circle at two points; P is the one inside the triangle, nearer BC (2.5 cm below A on the altitude).
(e) P, B, C: the centre is where the perpendicular bisectors of PB and BC meet; draw the circle through P, B, C. Radius ≈ 3.1 cm (calculation: altitude = √40 ≈ 6.32 cm, so P is ≈ 3.82 cm above BC; centre k above BC with k² + 9 = (3.82 − k)² gives k ≈ 0.74 cm, R = √(0.54 + 9) ≈ 3.09 cm).

marking_points.point: circle through P, B, C; radius ≈ 3.1 cm

questions.topic: Tangent and chord: similar triangles, area ratio
concepts: ratio of areas of similar triangles
questions.question:
AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. The tangent at B and chord AC extended meet at T.
(a) Prove that Δ ABC ~ Δ ATB.
(b) If AB = 20 cm, AC = 16 cm, find TB.
(c) Find A(Δ ABC) : A(Δ ATB).
questions.solution:
(a) In ΔABC and ΔATB: ∠BAC = ∠TAB (common); ∠ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle) and ∠ABT = 90° (radius ⊥ tangent), so ∠ACB = ∠ABT. Hence ΔABC ~ ΔATB (AA).
(b) Corresponding sides: AB/AT = AC/AB ⇒ 20/AT = 16/20 ⇒ AT = 25 cm. In right ΔABT, TB = √(AT² − AB²) = √(625 − 400) = 15 cm. (Also CT = 25 − 16 = 9 and TB² = CT × AT = 225.)
(c) A(ΔABC) : A(ΔATB) = AB² : AT² = 20² : 25² = 16 : 25.

marking_points.point: ∠A common and ∠ACB = ∠ABT = 90° with reasons ⇒ AA similarity

questions.topic: Selling shares and reinvesting: change in income
questions.question:
Arjav invested ₹24,000 in ₹50 shares at 4% discount giving 10% dividend. After one year he sold the shares at ₹65 and invested the proceeds (including his dividend) in ₹100 shares at ₹70 giving 11%. Calculate
(a) the change in annual dividend.
(b) the percentage increase in return on original investment.
questions.solution:
M.V. = 50 − 4% of 50 = ₹48. Shares = 24000/48 = 500. Dividend = 500 × 50 × 10/100 = ₹2500.
Sale proceeds + dividend = 500 × 65 + 2500 = 32500 + 2500 = ₹35,000. New shares = 35000/70 = 500. New dividend = 500 × 100 × 11/100 = ₹5500.
(a) Change (increase) in annual dividend = 5500 − 2500 = ₹3000.
(b) % increase in return on original investment = 3000/24000 × 100 = 12.5%.

questions.topic: Ogive: median, lower quartile, count above a value
questions.question:
A survey regarding height (in cm) of 60 boys belonging to class 10 of a school was conducted. The following data was recorded:
Height (in cm): 135-140 | 140-145 | 145-150 | 150-155 | 155-160 | 160-165 | 165-170
No. of boys: 4 | 8 | 20 | 14 | 7 | 6 | 1
Taking 2 cm = height of 10 cm along one axis and 2 cm = 10 boys along the other axis draw an ogive of the above distribution. Use the graph to estimate the following:
(i) the median
(ii) lower quartile
(iii) If height above 158 cm is considered as the tall boy of the class, find the number of boys in the class who are tall.
questions.solution:
Cumulative frequencies: 4, 12, 32, 46, 53, 59, 60. Plot (140, 4), (145, 12), (150, 32), (155, 46), (160, 53), (165, 59), (170, 60) with the curve starting at (135, 0); join by a smooth curve (kink on x-axis before 135).
(i) N = 60; median = N/2 = 30th term ⇒ from graph ≈ 149.5 cm.
(ii) Q₁ = N/4 = 15th term ⇒ ≈ 146 cm.
(iii) From 158 cm on the x-axis the ogive gives ≈ 50 boys of height ≤ 158 cm, so tall boys = 60 − 50 = 10.

marking_points.point: correct scale and plotting of points

questions.topic: Identity with square root
questions.question: Prove that √[(sec θ − 1)/(sec θ + 1)] = cosec θ − cot θ.
questions.solution: LHS = √[(sec θ − 1)²/((sec θ + 1)(sec θ − 1))] = √[(sec θ − 1)²/(sec²θ − 1)] = √[(sec θ − 1)²/tan²θ] = (sec θ − 1)/tan θ = ((1 − cos θ)/cos θ) × (cos θ/sin θ) = (1 − cos θ)/sin θ = 1/sin θ − cos θ/sin θ = cosec θ − cot θ = RHS.

marking_points.point: convert to (1 − cos θ)/sin θ = cosec θ − cot θ

questions.topic: Componendo and dividendo with surds
questions.question:
Using the properties of proportion, find the value of x (x > 0):
(2x + √(3x² + 1)) / (2x − √(3x² + 1)) = 15
questions.solution: By componendo and dividendo: 4x / (2√(3x² + 1)) = 16/14 ⇒ 2x/√(3x² + 1) = 8/7 ⇒ x/√(3x² + 1) = 4/7. Squaring: x²/(3x² + 1) = 16/49 ⇒ 49x² = 48x² + 16 ⇒ x² = 16 ⇒ x = ±4. Since x > 0, x = 4.

questions.topic: Cylinder inscribed in a sphere: remaining volume ratio
questions.question:
Two hemispheres are joined together to just cover a cylinder of height 8 cm and base radius 3 cm (the cylinder is inscribed in the sphere). Find
(a) the radius of the sphere
(b) the ratio of the volume of the remaining space to the volume of cylinder.
questions.solution:
(a) The centre of the sphere is the midpoint of the cylinder's axis; a rim point is 4 cm along the axis and 3 cm from it: R² = 3² + 4² = 25 ⇒ R = 5 cm.
(b) Volume of sphere = (4/3)π(125) = 500π/3; volume of cylinder = π(9)(8) = 72π. Remaining space = 500π/3 − 72π = 284π/3. Ratio = (284π/3) : 72π = 284 : 216 = 71 : 54.

questions.topic: Reflection in x = 0, invariant points, figure name
questions.question:
Use a graph sheet for this question. Take 2 cm = 1 unit along both the axes.
(a) Plot the following points A(0, −4), B(3, −2), C(1, 0), D(3, 2) & E(0, 1).
(b) Reflect the points B, C, D on the line x = 0 to the points H, G, F respectively and write their co-ordinates.
(c) Join the points A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H and assign a geometrical name to the figure.
(d) Name two invariant points under line x = 0.
(e) Which point is the image of A under reflection on the line BH? Write its coordinates.
questions.solution:
(a) Points plotted with the given scale.
(b) Reflection in x = 0 (y-axis): (x, y) → (−x, y). H(−3, −2), G(−1, 0), F(−3, 2).
(c) ABCDEFGH is an 8-sided figure (octagon) that is concave (irregular concave octagon, symmetric about the y-axis).
(d) A(0, −4) and E(0, 1) lie on x = 0, so they are invariant.
(e) BH is the line y = −2. Image of A(0, −4) in y = −2 is (0, 0), i.e. the origin O.

marking_points.point: points plotted and H(−3,−2), G(−1,0), F(−3,2)
image of A in BH (y = −2) is O(0, 0)

questions.topic: Median of equilateral triangle as perpendicular bisector
questions.question: In an equilateral triangle ABC, AD is the median. B = (6, 3), C = (8, 5). Find the equation of AD.
questions.solution: D is the midpoint of BC = ((6 + 8)/2, (3 + 5)/2) = (7, 4). In an equilateral triangle the median is also the altitude, so AD ⊥ BC. Slope of BC = (5 − 3)/(8 − 6) = 1 ⇒ slope of AD = −1. Equation: y − 4 = −1(x − 7) ⇒ x + y − 11 = 0.

questions.topic: Word problem: right triangle from a wire
questions.question: A 112 cm wire is bent to form a right angled triangle with hypotenuse 50 cm. Find the length of the sides of the triangle.
questions.solution: Sum of the other two sides = 112 − 50 = 62 cm. Let them be x and (62 − x). By Pythagoras: x² + (62 − x)² = 50² ⇒ 2x² − 124x + 3844 − 2500 = 0 ⇒ x² − 62x + 672 = 0 ⇒ (x − 14)(x − 48) = 0 ⇒ x = 14 or 48. The sides are 14 cm, 48 cm and 50 cm.

marking_points.point: other two sides x and 62 − x

questions.topic: Angles in semicircle, equal chords
questions.question: O is the centre of the circle and AB is a diameter. If AC = BD and ∠AOC = 68°, Find (a) ∠ABC (b) ∠BAD (c) ∠ABD.
questions.solution:
(a) ∠ABC = ½ ∠AOC = ½ × 68° = 34° (angle at centre is double the angle at the circumference on the same arc AC).
(b) AC = BD ⇒ equal chords subtend equal angles at the circumference: ∠BAD = ∠ABC = 34°.
(c) ∠ADB = 90° (angle in a semicircle). In ΔABD: ∠ABD = 180° − 90° − 34° = 56°.
questions.figure_desc: Circle with centre O, horizontal diameter AB; C and D on the lower arc with chords AC and BD marked equal, chords BC and AD drawn, ∠AOC = 68° marked at O.

questions.topic: Compound inequation in N with number line
questions.question:
Solve the given inequation and graph its solution on the real number line.
4x − 19 < 3x/5 − 2 ≤ −2/5 + x, x ∈ N
questions.solution: Left: 4x − 19 < (3x − 10)/5 ⇒ 20x − 95 < 3x − 10 ⇒ 17x < 85 ⇒ x < 5. Right: (3x − 10)/5 ≤ (5x − 2)/5 ⇒ 3x − 10 ≤ 5x − 2 ⇒ −8 ≤ 2x ⇒ x ≥ −4. So −4 ≤ x < 5; with x ∈ N, solution set = {1, 2, 3, 4}. On the number line, mark solid dots at 1, 2, 3, 4.

questions.topic: k-method proof
questions.question: If x/a = y/b = z/c then prove that: x²/a² + y²/b² + z²/c² = xy/ab + yz/bc + xz/ac
questions.solution: Let x/a = y/b = z/c = k ⇒ x = ak, y = bk, z = ck. LHS = a²k²/a² + b²k²/b² + c²k²/c² = 3k². RHS = (ak·bk)/ab + (bk·ck)/bc + (ak·ck)/ac = 3k². LHS = RHS. Hence proved.

marking_points.point: x = ak, y = bk, z = ck

questions.topic: Signboard on a building: two angles of elevation
questions.question:
A signboard is mounted on the top of the building. From a point P, 24 m away from the building, the angle of elevation of the top of the building is 30°, and the angle of elevation of the top of the sign board is 45°. Calculate
(a) the height of the sign board.
(b) the distance of the point P from the top of the signboard rounded off to 1 decimal place.
questions.solution:
Let AB = building, BE = building + signboard, PB = 24 m.
In ΔAPB: tan 30° = AB/24 ⇒ AB = 24/√3 = 8√3 ≈ 13.856 m. In ΔEPB: tan 45° = EB/24 ⇒ EB = 24 m.
(a) Height of signboard = 24 − 8√3 = 24 − 13.856 ≈ 10.14 m.
(b) sin 45° = EB/PE ⇒ PE = 24√2 ≈ 33.936 ≈ 33.9 m.
